Hi Carlos / Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap + concrete next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

Recap (short):
- We demoed the Redwood inference flow: hosted API + option for Dedicated pools.
- You indicated primary constraints: PII-handling for embeddings, SOC2 evidence, and predictable sub-100ms inference for short prompts.
- Integration topics we agreed to validate: SDK bootstrapping, auth/keying patterns, routing to cheaper model variants for non-sensitive traffic, and a reranker-based relevance pipeline for search.

Open technical decisions we should confirm:
1) Auth approach: you mentioned preferring automated service accounts over long-lived API keys. We flagged three options we recommend evaluating:
   - Short-lived JWT exchanged from your IdP (OIDC) -> Redwood token (best for SSO/least blast radius)
   - Scoped API keys with enforced IP + referrer rules (fastest to prototype)
   - Service account credentials with rotation + KMS (good middle ground for server-to-server)
2) Key rotation: target cadence and tooling (we recommend 30–90 day rotation with automated rotation hooks into your KMS and a grace-window policy).
3) Embeddings + rerank: we recommend storing embeddings in your vector DB and using a two-stage retrieval: semantic candidate generation (embeddings) + Redwood-hosted reranker or local re-ranker call for final ranking.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- BlueAxis: confirm which auth pattern you want the SE deep-dive to focus on ("OIDC/JWT exchange", "ephemeral service account tokens", or "managed API keys").
- BlueAxis: estimated average QPS and peak QPS for the initial pilot (very rough numbers are fine).
- Redwood: schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive (SE + infra) — propose Wed Sep 22, 10:00–11:00 PT.
- Redwood: share an integration checklist + sample code for short-lived tokens and embeddings flow (attached).

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (integration checklist), auth-patterns-compare.csv (pros/cons table)

If you want I can also open a quick security thread with our compliance team to address SOC2 request items up-front.

Thanks — Ben

Carlos / Emily — quick tech notes to help you pick the pattern for the deep-dive:

Short summary of pros/cons (opinionated):
- OIDC/JWT exchange (recommended when you have SSO): short-lived tokens minted by your IdP -> exchange endpoint in Redwood -> short TTL inference tokens. Pros: no long-lived credentials stored, integrates with your user provisioning. Cons: more initial setup and requires an exchange endpoint.
- Ephemeral service-account tokens: we can sign short-lived tokens for service accounts and push rotation hooks into your KMS. Pros: simpler for server-to-server, aligns with SOC2 controls if you prove rotation. Cons: still requires rotating secrets and a trust relationship.
- Scoped API keys: fastest POC but higher blast radius; must be used with strict network controls and usage limits.

Implementation notes we'll cover in the SE deep-dive:
1) Token exchange flow example (high-level):
   - BlueAxis backend authenticates to your IdP (client_assertion JWT)
   - IdP returns short-lived assertion -> call Redwood token-exchange endpoint -> get inference-token with TTL 5–15m
   - Use the inference-token in Authorization: Bearer <token> for SDK calls

2) Key rotation:
   - Rotate primary signing keys in KMS monthly; keep a 48-hour overlap window with old keys for in-flight token validation.
   - We provide hooks so your rotation event triggers a Redwood API to mark old keys expired.

3) Embeddings/rerank pattern we recommend:
   - Upsert document embeddings to your vector store with metadata including sensitivity tags.
   - For sensitive queries, route to a Dedicated pool pinned to a private deployment (if you elect Private mode).
   - For general traffic, route to a cost-optimized open model and then run a Redwood-hosted reranker on the top N candidates for final score.

I'll bring a sample key-rotation timeline and a short code snippet showing the exchange flow during the deep-dive.
